mechanism: Creatine supports ATP recycling. Berberine activates AMPK (energy sensor) and improves insulin sensitivity. Both enhance cellular energy but through different pathways.
dosing: Creatine: 5g daily. Berberine: 500mg 2-3x daily with meals.
physicianNote: I use this combination for patients with metabolic syndrome. Berberine addresses insulin resistance while creatine supports cellular energy recovery. Monitor blood glucose if diabetic.
safety: Berberine can cause GI upset. Start at 500mg daily and titrate. Creatine: avoid if CKD. No direct interaction between them.
references: Yin, J., et al. (2008). Efficacy of berberine in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus. Metabolism, 57(5), 712-717.|Kreider, R. B., et al. (2017). International Society of Sports Nutrition position stand: safety and efficacy of creatine supplementation.

mechanism: Omega-3 reduces inflammation via prostaglandin pathways. Curcumin inhibits NF-κB and COX-2. Together they create multi-pathway anti-inflammatory effect.
dosing: Omega-3: 2-3g EPA+DHA daily. Curcumin: 500-1000mg with black pepper (piperine enhances absorption).
physicianNote: This is my go-to combination for chronic inflammation. The synergy is well documented. Patients with joint pain, cardiovascular risk, or neuroinflammation see significant benefit.
safety: Both are blood thinners. If on warfarin, monitor INR. Take curcumin with fat for absorption. Generally very safe.
references: Chainani-Wu, N. (2003). Safety and anti-inflammatory activity of curcumin. Journal of Alternative and Complementary Medicine, 9(1), 161-168.

mechanism: Magnesium is required to convert vitamin D to its active form (calcitriol). Without adequate magnesium, vitamin D supplementation is ineffective.
dosing: Vitamin D: 2000-5000 IU daily. Magnesium: 300-400mg (glycinate or threonate form).
physicianNote: This is non-negotiable. I see patients with 'vitamin D resistance' who are simply magnesium deficient. Always supplement together.
safety: Magnesium can cause diarrhea >600mg. Vitamin D is fat soluble - take with meals. Monitor serum 25-OH vitamin D levels.
references: Uwitonze, A. M., & Razzaque, M. S. (2018). Role of magnesium in vitamin D activation and function. Journal of the American Osteopathic Association, 118(3), 181-189.

mechanism: Both activate AMPK and improve insulin sensitivity. Berberine acts as a 'natural metformin' but combining them may cause excessive glucose lowering.
dosing: Do not combine without physician supervision. Risk of hypoglycemia.
physicianNote: I occasionally use this combination in prediabetic patients who need aggressive intervention, but only with careful glucose monitoring. This is NOT a DIY protocol.
safety: Risk of hypoglycemia, GI upset, lactic acidosis (rare). Requires blood glucose monitoring and medical supervision.
references: Yin, J., et al. (2008). Efficacy of berberine in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus.

mechanism: Zinc and copper compete for absorption. High dose zinc causes copper deficiency (anemia, neurological damage). Ideal ratio is 10:1 zinc:copper.
dosing: If supplementing zinc >30mg daily, add 2-3mg copper. Or use a balanced multi-mineral.
physicianNote: I see copper deficiency regularly in patients mega-dosing zinc for immune support. Always maintain the 10:1 ratio.
safety: Excess zinc (>50mg daily) without copper causes anemia, neuropathy. Copper excess is toxic. Use balanced formulations.
references: Rostan, E. F., et al. (2002). Evidence supporting zinc as an important antioxidant for skin. International Journal of Dermatology, 41(9), 606-611.

mechanism: L-theanine (from green tea) increases alpha brain waves and GABA. Caffeine blocks adenosine receptors. Together: alertness without jitters.
dosing: Caffeine: 100-200mg. L-theanine: 200-400mg (2:1 ratio theanine:caffeine).
physicianNote: This is the 'focused calm' stack. I use it myself for clinical work. The synergy is well studied and highly effective for cognitive performance.
safety: Both are safe. L-theanine can cause drowsiness at very high doses (>600mg). Start with 200mg theanine + 100mg caffeine.
references: Haskell, C. F., et al. (2008). The effects of L-theanine, caffeine and their combination on cognition and mood. Biological Psychology, 77(2), 113-122.

mechanism: Vitamin D increases calcium absorption. Vitamin K2 directs calcium to bones (not arteries). Without K2, excess calcium deposits in soft tissue (vascular calcification).
dosing: Vitamin D: 2000-5000 IU daily. Vitamin K2 (MK-7): 100-200mcg daily.
physicianNote: This is critical for cardiovascular protection. I never prescribe vitamin D without K2. Prevents arterial calcification.
safety: Vitamin K2 interferes with warfarin. If on blood thinners, consult physician. Otherwise very safe.
references: Schurgers, L. J., et al. (2007). Vitamin K-containing dietary supplements: comparison of synthetic vitamin K1 and natto-derived menaquinone-7. Blood, 109(8), 3279-3283.

mechanism: Ashwagandha reduces cortisol (calming adaptogen). Rhodiola increases catecholamines (stimulating adaptogen). Together: balanced stress response.
dosing: Ashwagandha: 300-600mg daily (evening). Rhodiola: 200-400mg daily (morning).
physicianNote: I use this for patients with chronic stress and fatigue. Ashwagandha prevents burnout. Rhodiola provides energy. Timing is key.
safety: Ashwagandha can be sedating - dose evening. Rhodiola can be stimulating - dose morning. No direct interactions. Avoid rhodiola if on MAOIs.
references: Panossian, A., & Wikman, G. (2010). Effects of adaptogens on the central nervous system. Pharmaceuticals, 3(1), 188-224.

mechanism: Folate (B9) and B12 work synergistically in methylation. High folate without B12 masks B12 deficiency (causes irreversible nerve damage).
dosing: B12: 1000mcg (methylcobalamin). Folate: 400-800mcg (methylfolate form).
physicianNote: Never mega-dose folate without B12. I see neurological damage in vegans who supplement folic acid but neglect B12.
safety: High folic acid (synthetic form) can mask B12 deficiency. Use methylated forms (methylfolate, methylcobalamin). Very safe when balanced.
references: Aparicio-Ugarriza, R., et al. (2015). A review of the cut-off points for the diagnosis of vitamin B12 deficiency in the general population. Clinical Chemistry and Laboratory Medicine, 53(8), 1149-1159.

mechanism: Vitamin C converts non-heme iron (plant sources) from Fe3+ to Fe2+, increasing absorption by 3-4x. Critical for vegetarians/vegans.
dosing: Iron: 15-30mg with meals. Vitamin C: 500mg with iron dose.
physicianNote: If you are supplementing iron (especially plant-based), always take vitamin C. Absorption increases dramatically.
safety: Iron causes constipation and GI upset. Take with food. Avoid tea/coffee (tannins block absorption). Vitamin C enhances absorption. Do not exceed 45mg iron daily without medical supervision.
references: Teucher, B., et al. (2004). Enhancers of iron absorption: ascorbic acid and other organic acids. International Journal for Vitamin and Nutrition Research, 74(6), 403-419.

mechanism: Melatonin signals sleep onset. Magnesium relaxes muscles and nervous system. Together: improved sleep onset and quality.
dosing: Melatonin: 0.3-3mg 30 min before bed. Magnesium: 300-400mg 1-2hr before bed.
physicianNote: This is my first-line sleep stack. Start with magnesium alone. Add melatonin if needed. Most patients only need both for 2-4 weeks to reset sleep.
safety: Melatonin can cause grogginess (start at 0.3mg). Magnesium can cause diarrhea (use glycinate form). No interactions.
references: Held, K., et al. (2002). Oral Mg2+ supplementation reverses age-related neuroendocrine and sleep EEG changes in humans. Pharmacopsychiatry, 35(4), 135-143.

mechanism: ALA is a mitochondrial antioxidant. ALCAR transports fatty acids into mitochondria for energy production. Together: mitochondrial protection + fuel delivery.
dosing: ALA: 300-600mg daily. ALCAR: 500-1500mg daily.
physicianNote: This is the classic mitochondrial support combination. I use it for neuropathy, cognitive decline, and metabolic dysfunction.
safety: ALA can cause hypoglycemia in diabetics (monitor glucose). ALCAR can cause fishy body odor at high doses (genetic). Both are generally safe.
references: Hagen, T. M., et al. (2002). Feeding acetyl-L-carnitine and lipoic acid to old rats significantly improves metabolic function while decreasing oxidative stress. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 99(4), 1870-1875.

mechanism: Lysine and arginine compete for absorption. High lysine blocks arginine (needed for nitric oxide). High arginine can trigger herpes outbreaks (lysine suppresses it).
dosing: If supplementing for cold sores: Lysine 1000-3000mg, avoid arginine. If supplementing for NO/cardiovascular: Arginine 3-6g, normal lysine from diet.
physicianNote: These are antagonists. Choose one based on your goal. Do not mega-dose both simultaneously.
safety: Arginine can cause GI upset and lower blood pressure. Lysine is very safe. If prone to herpes, avoid high arginine foods (nuts, chocolate).
references: Griffith, R. S., et al. (1987). Success of L-lysine therapy in frequently recurrent herpes simplex infection. Dermatologica, 175(4), 183-190.

mechanism: Prebiotics are food for probiotics. Without prebiotics, probiotics do not colonize effectively. Together: synbiotic effect.
dosing: Probiotics: 10-50 billion CFU daily. Prebiotics: 5-10g daily (inulin, FOS, resistant starch).
physicianNote: I always prescribe these together. Probiotics alone often fail because the gut environment is not supportive. Prebiotics create the habitat.
safety: Start prebiotics slowly (can cause gas/bloating). Probiotics: choose multi-strain formulas. Generally very safe.
references: Gibson, G. R., et al. (2017). Expert consensus document: The International Scientific Association for Probiotics and Prebiotics (ISAPP) consensus statement on the definition and scope of prebiotics. Nature Reviews Gastroenterology & Hepatology, 14(8), 491-502.

mechanism: SAMe is a methyl donor (supports methylation). B-vitamins (B6, B9, B12) are cofactors for methylation. Together: enhanced methylation capacity.
dosing: SAMe: 400-800mg daily (morning). B-complex: 50-100mg B6, 400mcg methylfolate, 1000mcg methyl-B12.
physicianNote: SAMe is expensive. Optimize B-vitamins first (cheaper and often sufficient). Add SAMe if depression/joint pain persists.
safety: SAMe can be overstimulating (take morning). Avoid if bipolar (can trigger mania). B-vitamins are very safe. No direct interactions.
references: Papakostas, G. I., et al. (2010). S-adenosyl methionine (SAMe) augmentation of serotonin reuptake inhibitors for antidepressant nonresponders with major depressive disorder. American Journal of Psychiatry, 167(8), 942-948.

mechanism: Both are antioxidants with different mechanisms. Vitamin C is water soluble (intracellular). Quercetin is lipophilic (membrane protection). Together: comprehensive antioxidant coverage.
dosing: Vitamin C: 500-1000mg daily. Quercetin: 500-1000mg daily with fat.
physicianNote: This combination has shown particular benefit for immune support and histamine regulation. I use it for patients with allergies or chronic viral infections.
safety: Quercetin has mild blood thinning effects. High dose vitamin C (>2g) can cause diarrhea. Both are generally very safe.
references: Davis, J. M., et al. (2008). Quercetin reduces susceptibility to influenza infection. American Journal of Physiology-Regulatory, Integrative and Comparative Physiology, 295(2), R505-R509.

mechanism: Vitamin C is required for collagen synthesis (hydroxylation of proline and lysine). Without adequate vitamin C, collagen supplementation is ineffective.
dosing: Collagen: 10-20g daily. Vitamin C: 500-1000mg with collagen dose.
physicianNote: I see patients spending £50/month on collagen peptides but neglecting vitamin C. This is biochemically futile. Always supplement together.
safety: Collagen is tasteless protein (very safe). Vitamin C >2g can cause GI upset. Take collagen with vitamin C for maximum benefit.
references: Pullar, J. M., et al. (2017). The roles of vitamin C in skin health. Nutrients, 9(8), 866.

mechanism: Both thin blood (omega-3 via prostaglandin modulation, aspirin via COX inhibition). Combining increases bleeding risk.
dosing: If on aspirin therapy: Omega-3 1-2g max. Monitor for easy bruising.
physicianNote: I use this combination in high-risk cardiovascular patients, but only with careful monitoring. Do not self-prescribe if on aspirin.
safety: Increased bleeding risk, particularly GI bleeding. If you bruise easily, reduce omega-3 dose. Consult physician if on aspirin therapy.
references: Bays, H. E. (2007). Safety considerations with omega-3 fatty acid therapy. American Journal of Cardiology, 99(6), S35-S43.

mechanism: Curcumin (from turmeric) has 1% bioavailability. Piperine (from black pepper) inhibits glucuronidation, increasing curcumin absorption by 2000%.
dosing: Turmeric: 500-1000mg curcumin. Black pepper: 5-10mg piperine (or 1/4 tsp black pepper).
physicianNote: This is non-negotiable. Turmeric without piperine is mostly wasted. Look for curcumin supplements with added black pepper extract.
safety: Both are safe. Turmeric can thin blood mildly. High doses (>3g) can cause GI upset. Black pepper enhances absorption of many compounds.
references: Shoba, G., et al. (1998). Influence of piperine on the pharmacokinetics of curcumin in animals and human volunteers. Planta Medica, 64(4), 353-356.

mechanism: CBD modulates serotonin and GABA receptors (anxiolytic). Melatonin signals circadian rhythm. Together: reduced sleep latency and improved sleep quality.
dosing: CBD: 10-25mg sublingual 1hr before bed. Melatonin: 0.3-3mg 30min before bed.
physicianNote: This works exceptionally well for anxiety-driven insomnia. Start with melatonin alone. Add CBD if rumination persists.
safety: CBD can cause drowsiness (intended effect). Melatonin can cause morning grogginess (start at 0.3mg). CBD may interact with CYP450 drugs.
references: Carlini, E. A., & Cunha, J. M. (1981). Hypnotic and antiepileptic effects of cannabidiol. Journal of Clinical Pharmacology, 21(S1), 417S-427S.

mechanism: Vitamin D increases calcium absorption in the gut. Without vitamin D, dietary calcium is poorly absorbed (10-15% vs 30-40% with D).
dosing: Calcium: 500-1000mg with meals. Vitamin D: 2000-5000 IU daily.
physicianNote: Do not mega-dose calcium without vitamin D. Also add vitamin K2 to prevent vascular calcification.
safety: Excess calcium (>2500mg) increases kidney stone risk. Always take with vitamin D and K2. Spread calcium doses throughout day.
references: Holick, M. F. (2007). Vitamin D deficiency. New England Journal of Medicine, 357(3), 266-281.

mechanism: Cordyceps increases ATP production and oxygen utilization. Rhodiola enhances stress resilience and reduces fatigue. Together: energy + endurance.
dosing: Cordyceps: 1-3g daily (morning). Rhodiola: 200-400mg daily (morning).
physicianNote: This is my athletic performance stack. Particularly effective for endurance athletes or patients recovering from chronic fatigue.
safety: Both are stimulating (dose morning). Can cause jitteriness if combined with caffeine. Avoid rhodiola if on MAOIs.
references: Chen, S., et al. (2010). Effect of Cs-4 (Cordyceps sinensis) on exercise performance in healthy older subjects. Journal of Alternative and Complementary Medicine, 16(5), 585-590.

mechanism: Lions mane stimulates NGF (nerve growth factor) for neurogenesis. Bacopa enhances acetylcholine signaling. Together: structural + functional brain support.
dosing: Lions mane: 500-1000mg daily. Bacopa: 300-450mg daily (standardized to 50% bacosides).
physicianNote: This is the cognitive longevity stack. Takes 4-8 weeks to see benefits (not acute). For memory, focus, and neuroprotection.
safety: Both are very safe. Bacopa can cause GI upset (take with food). Lions mane is essentially a culinary mushroom.
references: Mori, K., et al. (2009). Improving effects of the mushroom Yamabushitake on mild cognitive impairment. Phytotherapy Research, 23(3), 367-372.

mechanism: GABA is the primary inhibitory neurotransmitter. L-theanine enhances GABA receptor sensitivity and increases alpha brain waves. Together: calm without sedation.
dosing: GABA: 250-750mg. L-theanine: 200-400mg.
physicianNote: Oral GABA has poor blood brain barrier penetration, so effects are likely via gut-brain axis. Works well for stress reduction.
safety: Both are very safe. High dose GABA (>3g) can cause paradoxical anxiety. L-theanine can cause drowsiness >600mg.
references: Abdou, A. M., et al. (2006). Relaxation and immunity enhancement effects of γ-aminobutyric acid administration in humans. BioFactors, 26(3), 201-208.

mechanism: Both are serotonin precursors. 5-HTP is one step closer to serotonin than tryptophan. Combining them can cause serotonin syndrome (dangerous).
dosing: Use ONE or the other. 5-HTP: 50-100mg daily. Tryptophan: 500-1000mg daily. Never combine.
physicianNote: This is a common mistake. Choose 5-HTP for faster effect or tryptophan for gentler, sustained support. Do not take both.
safety: Risk of serotonin syndrome if combined (agitation, hyperthermia, muscle rigidity). Avoid if on SSRIs. Choose one precursor only.
references: Birdsall, T. C. (1998). 5-Hydroxytryptophan: a clinically-effective serotonin precursor. Alternative Medicine Review, 3(4), 271-280.

mechanism: Boswellia (frankincense) inhibits 5-LOX (leukotriene pathway). Fish oil inhibits COX-2 (prostaglandin pathway). Together: dual anti-inflammatory action.
dosing: Boswellia: 300-500mg (standardized to 60% boswellic acids). Fish oil: 2-3g EPA+DHA.
physicianNote: This is particularly effective for joint inflammation and inflammatory bowel disease. Synergistic pathways = greater efficacy.
safety: Both are blood thinners. Monitor if on warfarin. Boswellia can cause mild GI upset. Fish oil: take with meals to avoid fishy burps.
references: Kimmatkar, N., et al. (2003). Efficacy and tolerability of Boswellia serrata extract in treatment of osteoarthritis of knee. Phytomedicine, 10(1), 3-7.

mechanism: St Johns Wort induces CYP450 enzymes and has SSRI-like effects. Combining with pharmaceutical SSRIs causes serotonin syndrome.
dosing: Never combine. Use one or the other. Consult physician before stopping SSRIs.
physicianNote: This is dangerous. I see this mistake regularly. St Johns Wort is a powerful herb with real drug interactions. Not a supplement to DIY.
safety: Serotonin syndrome risk (life-threatening). St Johns Wort also reduces efficacy of birth control, warfarin, and many other drugs. Physician supervision required.
references: Linde, K., et al. (2008). St John's wort for major depression. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, (4).

mechanism: Green tea contains EGCG (antioxidant) and ~25mg caffeine per cup. Adding more caffeine enhances fat oxidation and alertness.
dosing: Green tea extract: 400-500mg EGCG. Caffeine: 100-200mg.
physicianNote: This is the classic fat loss and nootropic stack. EGCG + caffeine increases metabolic rate by 4-5%. Effective but not magic.
safety: Can cause jitteriness, insomnia if dosed too late. Limit total caffeine to <400mg daily. Green tea extract can affect liver enzymes at very high doses (>800mg EGCG).
references: Dulloo, A. G., et al. (1999). Efficacy of a green tea extract rich in catechin polyphenols and caffeine in increasing 24-h energy expenditure and fat oxidation. American Journal of Clinical Nutrition, 70(6), 1040-1045.

mechanism: Both are algae with different nutrient profiles. Spirulina is protein-rich (60-70%). Chlorella has broken cell wall for heavy metal binding. Together: nutrition + detox.
dosing: Spirulina: 3-5g daily. Chlorella: 3-5g daily.
physicianNote: I use this for patients seeking plant-based protein and gentle heavy metal chelation. Start low (both can cause GI upset initially).
safety: Both can cause nausea if started at full dose. Chlorella can cause green stools (normal). Spirulina is high in iodine (caution if hyperthyroid).
references: Yamane, Y., et al. (1988). Effect of chlorella on colonic microbiota. Biotherapy, 1(4), 251-259.

mechanism: Phosphatidylserine is a membrane phospholipid (cognitive function). Omega-3 provides DHA (brain structure). Together: membrane fluidity + neuroprotection.
dosing: Phosphatidylserine: 100-300mg daily. Omega-3: 1-2g DHA daily.
physicianNote: This combination has strong evidence for cognitive decline prevention and ADHD symptom reduction. Works best over 8-12 weeks.
safety: Both are very safe. High dose omega-3 (>3g) can thin blood. Phosphatidylserine: take earlier in day (can be stimulating for some).
references: Kato-Kataoka, A., et al. (2010). Soybean-derived phosphatidylserine improves memory function of the elderly Japanese subjects with memory complaints. Journal of Clinical Biochemistry and Nutrition, 47(3), 246-255.

mechanism: Elderberry has antiviral properties (inhibits viral neuraminidase). Zinc is required for immune cell function. Together: antiviral + immune support.
dosing: Elderberry: 300-600mg extract during illness. Zinc: 15-30mg daily (or 50mg lozenges during acute illness).
physicianNote: This is my acute viral illness protocol. Start at first symptoms. Elderberry reduces duration by 2-4 days in studies.
safety: Zinc lozenges can cause nausea on empty stomach. Elderberry is very safe. Do not mega-dose zinc >50mg long-term (copper depletion).
references: Zakay-Rones, Z., et al. (2004). Randomized study of the efficacy and safety of oral elderberry extract in the treatment of influenza A and B virus infections. Journal of International Medical Research, 32(2), 132-140.

mechanism: Ginkgo increases cerebral blood flow (vascular). Bacopa enhances acetylcholine and BDNF (neurochemical). Together: blood flow + neurotransmitter support.
dosing: Ginkgo: 120-240mg daily (standardized extract). Bacopa: 300-450mg daily.
physicianNote: This is for cognitive performance and memory. Ginkgo works acutely (days). Bacopa requires 8-12 weeks. Use together for best results.
safety: Ginkgo is a blood thinner (caution with warfarin). Bacopa can cause GI upset. Both are generally safe but start one at a time.
references: Mix, J. A., & Crews, W. D. (2002). A double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized trial of Ginkgo biloba extract EGb 761 in a sample of cognitively intact older adults. Human Psychopharmacology, 17(6), 267-277.

mechanism: Beta-alanine increases muscle carnosine (buffering lactic acid). Creatine recycles ATP. Together: endurance + power.
dosing: Beta-alanine: 3-6g daily (divided doses). Creatine: 5g daily.
physicianNote: This is the classic sports performance stack. Beta-alanine takes 4 weeks to saturate muscle carnosine. Creatine works within days.
safety: Beta-alanine causes harmless paresthesia (tingling). Creatine: ensure hydration. Both are safe for long-term use.
references: Hoffman, J., et al. (2006). Effect of creatine and beta-alanine supplementation on performance and endocrine responses in strength/power athletes. International Journal of Sport Nutrition and Exercise Metabolism, 16(4), 430-446.

mechanism: Digestive enzymes break down food (proteases, lipases, amylases). Probiotics restore gut flora. Together: digestion + microbiome support.
dosing: Digestive enzymes: with meals. Probiotics: 10-50 billion CFU away from meals.
physicianNote: I use this for SIBO, IBS, and post-antibiotic recovery. Enzymes provide immediate relief. Probiotics restore long-term balance.
safety: Start probiotics slowly (can cause gas/bloating initially). Digestive enzymes are very safe. Choose broad-spectrum enzyme formulas.
references: Money, M. E., & Camilleri, M. (2012). Review: management of postprandial diarrhea syndrome. American Journal of Medicine, 125(6), 538-544.

mechanism: Glutamine is fuel for intestinal cells (enterocytes). Probiotics colonize the gut lining. Together: gut barrier repair + microbiome.
dosing: Glutamine: 5-10g daily (divided doses). Probiotics: 10-50 billion CFU.
physicianNote: This is my leaky gut protocol. Glutamine heals the intestinal lining. Probiotics restore the ecosystem. Works synergistically.
safety: Glutamine is very safe (amino acid). Can be stimulating for some (dose earlier in day). Probiotics: start low to avoid GI upset.
references: Zuhl, M., et al. (2014). The effects of acute oral glutamine supplementation on exercise-induced gastrointestinal permeability and heat shock protein expression. Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition, 11(1), 8.

mechanism: Milk thistle (silymarin) protects liver cells and increases glutathione. NAC is a direct glutathione precursor. Together: liver protection + antioxidant support.
dosing: Milk thistle: 200-400mg (standardized to 70-80% silymarin). NAC: 600-1200mg daily.
physicianNote: This is the liver protection stack. Particularly useful for patients on hepatotoxic medications or alcohol exposure.
safety: Both are very safe. Milk thistle can cause mild GI upset. NAC: take with food to minimize nausea.
references: Polyak, S. J., et al. (2007). Identification of hepatoprotective flavonolignans from silymarin. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 104(13), 5995-5999.

mechanism: Valerian enhances GABA (sedative). Lemon balm has mild anxiolytic effects. Together: sleep onset + sleep maintenance.
dosing: Valerian: 300-600mg 1hr before bed. Lemon balm: 300-500mg 1hr before bed.
physicianNote: This is gentler than melatonin for some patients. Works well for stress-driven insomnia. Takes 2-4 weeks for full effect.
safety: Valerian can cause morning grogginess (start at 300mg). Lemon balm is very safe. Both can potentiate sedatives (caution with benzos).
references: Cerny, A., & Schmid, K. (1999). Tolerability and efficacy of valerian/lemon balm in healthy volunteers. Fitoterapia, 70(3), 221-228.

mechanism: Maca supports adrenal function and libido (non-hormonal). Tribulus may increase testosterone precursors. Together: energy + hormonal balance.
dosing: Maca: 1.5-3g daily. Tribulus: 250-750mg daily (standardized to 40% saponins).
physicianNote: Evidence for tribulus is mixed. Maca has better data for libido and energy. I use both for andropause symptoms.
safety: Both are safe. Maca can be stimulating (dose morning). Tribulus: avoid if prostate issues (theoretical concern).
references: Gonzales, G. F., et al. (2002). Effect of Lepidium meyenii (MACA) on sexual desire and its absent relationship with serum testosterone levels in adult healthy men. Andrologia, 34(6), 367-372.

mechanism: Both are required for thyroid hormone synthesis. Too much selenium without iodine, or vice versa, impairs thyroid function.
dosing: Selenium: 100-200mcg daily. Iodine: 150-300mcg daily (or from iodized salt).
physicianNote: I see subclinical hypothyroidism improve when both are optimized. Do not mega-dose iodine (>500mcg) without selenium.
safety: Excess iodine (>1000mcg) can trigger hyperthyroidism. Excess selenium (>400mcg) causes selenosis (hair loss, nausea). Balance is critical.
references: Ventura, M., et al. (2017). Selenium and thyroid disease: from pathophysiology to treatment. International Journal of Endocrinology, 2017.

mechanism: Glucosamine provides building blocks for cartilage (glycosaminoglycans). Chondroitin inhibits cartilage breakdown enzymes. Together: synthesis + protection.
dosing: Glucosamine: 1500mg daily. Chondroitin: 1200mg daily.
physicianNote: This is the classic joint health stack. Takes 8-12 weeks to see benefits. Evidence is modest but some patients respond well.
safety: Both are very safe. Glucosamine can raise blood sugar slightly in diabetics (monitor). Chondroitin: rare allergic reactions.
references: Clegg, D. O., et al. (2006). Glucosamine, chondroitin sulfate, and the two in combination for painful knee osteoarthritis. New England Journal of Medicine, 354(8), 795-808.

mechanism: Both are xanthophyll carotenoids that accumulate in the macula (retina). Lutein is in peripheral macula, zeaxanthin in center. Together: comprehensive macular protection.
dosing: Lutein: 10-20mg daily. Zeaxanthin: 2-4mg daily.
physicianNote: This is evidence-based macular degeneration prevention. AREDS2 trial showed clear benefit. Start early (40s) for best results.
safety: Both are very safe. Fat soluble (take with meals). Can cause yellowing of skin at very high doses (harmless).
references: Age-Related Eye Disease Study 2 Research Group. (2013). Lutein + zeaxanthin and omega-3 fatty acids for age-related macular degeneration. JAMA, 309(19), 2005-2015.

mechanism: Citrulline converts to arginine in kidneys (avoids first-pass metabolism). Arginine is substrate for nitric oxide. Together: sustained NO production.
dosing: Citrulline: 3-6g daily. Arginine: 3-6g daily (or use citrulline alone for better effect).
physicianNote: Citrulline is actually superior to arginine for NO production (better bioavailability). Combining them provides immediate + sustained effect.
safety: Both are safe. High dose arginine can cause GI upset. Citrulline is better tolerated. Both lower blood pressure (caution if hypotensive).
references: Schwedhelm, E., et al. (2008). Pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic properties of oral L-citrulline and L-arginine. Amino Acids, 34(3), 413-420.

mechanism: Schisandra protects liver and enhances mental performance. Eleuthero (Siberian ginseng) increases stress resilience. Together: adaptogenic synergy.
dosing: Schisandra: 500-2000mg daily. Eleuthero: 300-1200mg daily.
physicianNote: This is the Russian adaptogen stack (studied in cosmonauts). Enhances endurance and cognitive performance under stress.
safety: Both are stimulating (dose morning). Can cause insomnia if dosed late. Avoid eleuthero if hypertensive (can raise BP).
references: Panossian, A., & Wikman, G. (2008). Pharmacology of Schisandra chinensis Bail. Journal of Ethnopharmacology, 118(2), 183-212.

mechanism: Tyrosine is precursor to dopamine. Mucuna provides L-DOPA (immediate dopamine precursor). Together: substrate + direct precursor.
dosing: N-Acetyl Tyrosine: 500-1000mg morning. Mucuna: 100-300mg (standardized to 15% L-DOPA).
physicianNote: This is for dopamine deficiency (low motivation, focus, pleasure). Powerful but should be used cautiously. Not for long-term daily use without medical supervision.
safety: Mucuna can cause nausea (start low). Can interfere with Parkinson's medications. Both can cause overstimulation. Cycle use (5 days on, 2 off).
references: Katzenschlager, R., et al. (2004). Mucuna pruriens in Parkinson's disease: a double blind clinical and pharmacological study. Journal of Neurology, Neurosurgery & Psychiatry, 75(12), 1672-1677.

mechanism: Resveratrol activates SIRT1 (longevity). Pterostilbene is methylated resveratrol (better bioavailability). Together: immediate + sustained sirtuin activation.
dosing: Resveratrol: 250-500mg. Pterostilbene: 50-100mg.
physicianNote: Pterostilbene has 4x better bioavailability than resveratrol. Combining them provides both immediate and sustained effects.
safety: Both are safe. Can cause mild GI upset. Theoretical concern with estrogen-receptor positive cancers (consult oncologist).
references: McCormack, D., & McFadden, D. (2013). A review of pterostilbene antioxidant activity and disease modification. Oxidative Medicine and Cellular Longevity, 2013.

mechanism: Astaxanthin is lipophilic antioxidant (membrane protection). Vitamin E prevents lipid peroxidation. Together: synergistic antioxidant effect.
dosing: Astaxanthin: 4-12mg daily with fat. Vitamin E: 200-400 IU (mixed tocopherols).
physicianNote: This is for skin health, eye health, and cardiovascular protection. Astaxanthin is one of the most potent antioxidants.
safety: Both are fat soluble (take with meals). High dose vitamin E (>400 IU) may increase bleeding risk. Use mixed tocopherols, not alpha only.
references: Tominaga, K., et al. (2012). Cosmetic benefits of astaxanthin on humans subjects. Acta Biochimica Polonica, 59(1), 43-47.

mechanism: Berberine activates AMPK (glucose uptake). ALA improves insulin signaling and mitochondrial function. Together: enhanced glucose metabolism.
dosing: Berberine: 500mg 2-3x daily. ALA: 300-600mg daily.
physicianNote: This is my natural blood sugar management protocol. Works as well as metformin in some patients. Requires 8-12 weeks to see full effect.
safety: Berberine causes GI upset (start low). ALA can cause hypoglycemia in diabetics (monitor glucose). Both are generally safe.
references: Zhang, H., et al. (2008). Berberine lowers blood glucose in type 2 diabetes mellitus patients through increasing insulin receptor expression. Metabolism, 57(5), 712-717.

mechanism: Both are citrus flavonoids that strengthen vein walls (venotropic). Used for varicose veins and hemorrhoids. Together: additive vascular benefit.
dosing: Hesperidin: 500mg daily. Diosmin: 450mg daily.
physicianNote: This is micronized purified flavonoid fraction (MPFF) used in Europe for chronic venous insufficiency. Effective but underutilized in US.
safety: Both are very safe. Can cause mild GI upset. Particularly effective for leg swelling and varicose vein symptoms.
references: Rabe, E., & Pannier, F. (2012). Clinical, aetiological, anatomical and pathological classification in patients with chronic venous disorders. Phlebology, 27(3), 23-27.

mechanism: Policosanol may affect cholesterol. Red yeast rice contains natural statins (monacolin K). Combining increases statin exposure.
dosing: Use one or the other, not both. Red yeast rice: 1200-2400mg (containing 5-10mg monacolin K).
physicianNote: Red yeast rice is essentially a low-dose statin. Treat it as such. Monitor liver enzymes. Policosanol evidence is controversial.
safety: Red yeast rice: same side effects as statins (muscle pain, liver issues). Deplete CoQ10 (supplement 100-200mg). Policosanol is safer but less effective.
references: Becker, D. J., et al. (2009). Red yeast rice for dyslipidemia in statin-intolerant patients. Annals of Internal Medicine, 150(12), 830-839.
